editorial:
Imagine waking up in the middle of the giant, noisy maze that is Mexico City. You are thrown into the lives of three total strangers who couldn't be more different. You have El Jairo, a guy who is convinced aliens are coming for him; Claudia, who is struggling with a secret porn addiction; and Juvenico, an old teacher who feels like the world has left him behind. It feels like a colorful, messy urban fable where everyone is just trying to survive their own weird habits while navigating the crowded streets. The vibe is lighthearted but has some sad moments that make the characters feel like real people you might actually meet on the street.

What really works here is the acting, especially how the cast makes these oddball characters feel lovable. The pacing is steady, and watching their lives slowly drift toward each other keeps you interested. While some parts of the story might feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy quirky character studies, you should definitely check this out. Since it is a hidden gem, you might want to look for it on a streaming service like Prime Video in 4K Ultra HD for the best colors, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up when the three characters finally cross paths in a way that feels like fate. After spending the whole film in their own little worlds, their meeting shows that everyone is lonely in a big city. They find a strange kind of comfort in each other's eccentricities. It ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that no matter how weird you are, you can still find a place where you belong.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird characters and stories about city life.
